scene_translation: The bartender continued speaking slowly, polishing a glass. 'Your grandmother, you see — she used to come here every month. She'd always sit in the same seat and order the same thing.' Testo suddenly noticed a worn envelope sitting at the far end of the counter. 'I've been holding onto it, all this time. I figured someone would come to collect it. Testo-san, I was told to give it to you.' On the front of the envelope, in an unfamiliar hand, was written only: 'To Testo.'
grammar_note: 【はずだ】expresses a reasonable expectation or logical conclusion — something 'should be' or 'is supposed to be' the case. Here: 誰かが取りに来るはずだと思っていた — 'I believed someone was sure to come and collect it.' It carries a sense of quiet certainty based on prior knowledge or instruction, which fits the bartender's long wait perfectly. Compare with でしょう (softer, more tentative guess) — はずだ implies firmer personal conviction.

mystery_memo: The central mystery deepens significantly: the grandmother was a regular at this unmapped bar, and had left a sealed envelope addressed specifically to the player — suggesting she anticipated their arrival long before the events of scene 1. The bartender (friendly, warm, clearly loyal to the grandmother's memory) has now handed over the key item: the envelope. Contents unknown. The woman in blue has not appeared; she may be connected to the grandmother. The envelope is now in the player's inventory and its contents will drive the next phase of the mystery.
